defaults.permitted_development: In Wales, rooflights and similar roof alterations are usually permitted development where they do not project more than 150 millimetres from the existing roof plane, do not rise above the highest part of the roof and do not fall within a protected-area restriction that removes the right.

rules.height_rules: Keep the rooflight within 150 millimetres of the existing roof plane and below the highest part of the roof.
rules.depth_rules: Projection rather than room depth is the key Welsh measurement for rooflights.
rules.boundary_rules: Privacy is the main boundary issue. Side-facing windows in the side elevation of a dwellinghouse that is within 10.5 metres of a side boundary should be obscure-glazed and non-opening.
rules.roof_rules: The safest Welsh design is a low-profile rooflight that reads as a modest alteration to the existing roof rather than a roof enlargement. Protected areas can remove the normal rooflight right altogether.
rules.materials_rules: The appearance of the materials used should, as far as possible, match the appearance of those used on the existing roof.

rules.permitted_development: Welsh permitted development can usually cover a modest rooflight where the unit stays close to the roof slope, remains below the highest part of the roof and avoids the protected-area restrictions that apply to some visible roof work.

rules.height_rules: The main Welsh limits are simple: no more than 150 millimetres proud of the roof plane and never above the highest part of the roof.
rules.depth_rules: Projection rather than room depth is the key Welsh measurement for rooflights.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary concerns usually arise from side-facing openings. Welsh guidance expects obscure glazing and no opening parts in the sensitive side-elevation scenario.
rules.roof_rules: Roof form matters because Welsh rooflight rights do not extend to bulkier roof enlargements. Keep the unit flush or low-profile and be careful in protected areas.
rules.materials_rules: Welsh guidance expects roof alterations to sit comfortably with the existing roof, so discreet frame colours, modest flashings and matching surrounding materials are usually the safest choice.

rules.depth_rules: There is no extension-style depth allowance for a Welsh rooflight; the practical test is how shallowly it sits on the roof.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary concerns usually arise from side-facing openings. Welsh guidance expects obscure glazing and no opening parts in the sensitive side-elevation scenario.
rules.roof_rules: A small rooflight is usually fine in Wales when it stays subordinate to the roof slope. Prominent roof changes on protected-area elevations are much more likely to need permission.
rules.materials_rules: The appearance of the materials used should, as far as possible, match the appearance of those used on the existing roof.

restrictions.listed_building: In Eryri, works to the interior or exterior of a listed building can require listed building consent, so do not rely on normal householder assumptions without checking first.

rules.permitted_development: Welsh permitted development can usually cover a modest rooflight where the unit stays close to the roof slope, remains below the highest part of the roof and avoids the protected-area restrictions that apply to some visible roof work.

rules.height_rules: Keep the rooflight within 150 millimetres of the existing roof plane and below the highest part of the roof.
rules.depth_rules: Projection rather than room depth is the key Welsh measurement for rooflights.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary concerns usually arise from side-facing openings. Welsh guidance expects obscure glazing and no opening parts in the sensitive side-elevation scenario.
rules.roof_rules: A small rooflight is usually fine in Wales when it stays subordinate to the roof slope. Prominent roof changes on protected-area elevations are much more likely to need permission.
rules.materials_rules: Welsh guidance expects roof alterations to sit comfortably with the existing roof, so discreet frame colours, modest flashings and matching surrounding materials are usually the safest choice.

restrictions.conservation_area: Within Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, conservation area and protected landscape controls can narrow normal householder rights and make formal checking especially important.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent may still be required in Pembrokeshire Coast National Park even where a proposal appears small or would normally be treated as householder work.
